topics: Performance wins: kernel improvements and batching
header: Date: 2026-08-28 | Time: 10:00 PT | Duration: 62 minutes | Attendees: ~150 Redwood employees (leadership on stage)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining the August all-hands. quick note, recordings and slides will be in the #all-hands channel after. um let's dive in. we had a strong month; Rajesh will kick off with infra and perf, then Caroline on product, hiring from Sara and then Q&A.

[00:35] Rajesh: hey everyone, quick update on serving runtime. we've rolled a set of kernel changes that, on average, reduce tail latency by about 12 to 18% for our 8k context models. these are the attention fusion kernels and a couple of memcopy reductions. some of the numbers are still a bit noisy because of the perf jobs but Tom and the infra team have done a great job.

[01:10] Tom: yeah, to add — continuous batching improvements and better KV cache reuse (sometimes the transcripts say KV cash, ignore that) reduced token cost by roughly 7% on our hosted tier; Dedicated customers are seeing the biggest delta because they have predictable throughput.

[01:45] Maya: great, real impact on cost for customers is the story here. Luis, quick commercial signal?

[01:55] Luis: we closed three mid-market customers this month and a pilot with a large finserv firm going into a dedicated POC. pipeline is healthy. Pricing tweaks we shipped in July have helped margins — nothing dramatic but incremental.

[02:20] Caroline: product updates — sequence of releases: 1) Redwood Optimize v0.9 shipped internal alpha for model recommendations, 2) Private has a GA checklist we're working and we've done two private installs for customers in regulated sectors, 3) streaming and function-calling improvements for chat that cut down the number of dropped events. note: we're still validating some edge cases in region routing where fallback to cheaper model variants caused slightly different responses — eval team is on it.

[03:05] Employee (Engineering): can you clarify Private GA timing?

[03:10] Caroline: aim for GA by mid-September; dependency is final KMS/HSM integration and a runbook from security. that'll be the gating items.

[03:30] Sara: hiring — we're adding 22 roles this quarter across infra, product, and sales. interview loop updates: please use the new rubric in Greenhouse, and interview feedback deadlines now 72 hours. also new parental leave policy goes into effect Sep 1.

[04:05] Maya: finance snapshot — we remain within plan for burn. revenue is up quarter-over-quarter; a reminder that our play is still to balance growth and margin neutrality for the next two quarters while we scale Private.

[04:40] Rajesh: ops note — we've tightened runbook automation; our mean time to respond for infra incidents dropped by ~20% since May. the incident where a training-vm leaked a GPU was contained, lessons learned documented.

[05:10] Q&A section begins.

[05:18] Employee (Data Scientist): are there plans to open-source any of the kernel work?

[05:25] Rajesh: good question. some of the optimization work is upstreamable but not everything — a mix. we'll post a list of candidate improvements.

[05:45] Employee (Sales): any change to our go-to-market messaging for Dedicated vs hosted?

[05:52] Luis: yes — emphasize predictable throughput and SLAs for Dedicated; hosted for quick wins and dev velocity. also new collateral is in the Sales Drive folder.

[06:20] Tom: small tech detail — we've improved quantization profiles; for certain workloads using 4-bit quant we see 30% cost reduction but a small hit in generation quality for long-form summarization tasks; guidance coming in the docs.

[07:00] Employee (Support): security questions from a customer—what's the status on SOC 2 and ISO?

[07:08] Kevin: security update — SOC 2 in final review, expected attestation in Q4; ISO gaps are near-closed pending docs. audit logs and SSO improvements shipped in July.

[07:40] Maya: let's talk roadmap priorities: 1) stabilize Private GA, 2) expand Dedicated capacity with better autoscaling policies, 3) Improve Optimize recommendations, 4) invest in observability/trace tooling that ties regressions back to prompt sets.

[08:10] Employee (Product): can we get more detail on observability investment?

[08:15] Caroline: yep — new tracing hooks planned for Q4, and we're building a regression alerting pipeline that maps eval sets to production endpoints; this will automate rollbacks for bad model updates.

[08:45] Rajesh: small demo: showed a dashboard snippet (link in chat) with per-route latency and token cost. note: dropdown had a mis-typo in the demo deck — will fix.

[09:30] Employee (Engineer): any changes to release cadence?

[09:35] Tom: we'll keep fortnightly releases for infra-critical stuff and monthly for product features, with emergency patches as needed.

[10:00] Mid-meeting check: cross-team shoutouts and kudos.

[10:20] Shoutout: infra on-call rotation improvement (nominated Tom and team) — applause.

[10:45] Employee (Eng): question about model catalog — are we curating more open models or focusing on few high-perf variants?

[10:55] Caroline: both — curate a small set of verified models and maintain a broader catalog for experimental use. quality profiles will be visible in the console.

[11:20] Employee (Research): how aggressive on quantization recommendations? are we auto-applying them?

[11:30] Rajesh: not auto-applying — we'll recommend and optionally run jobs in staging for customers who opt-in. also the recommendation engine in Optimize will suggest by workload.

[12:05] Question about Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity pricing.

[12:12] Luis: burst capacity is priced separately; sales to share the updated pricing sheet. customers like the predictability but want easy burst ops.

[12:40] Security question from legal: retention policies and data residency updates.

[12:48] Kevin: retention defaults remain 30 days for hosted; Dedicated and Private can configure retention. data residency options expanding to eu-west-3 and ap-southeast-1 next quarter.

[13:15] Employee (Sales Engineer): any updates on partner integrations?

[13:20] Luis: signed two new partners for reseller channels in EMEA. working on marketplace listings with cloud providers.

[13:45] Open floor: miscellaneous updates.

[14:00] Maya: hiring push — we need help from ICs on interviewing; please volunteer. also reminder about the company offsite in October.

[14:25] Employee (IC): question about roadmap prioritization — how do we decide between invest in observability vs quantization research?

[14:32] Maya: decision framework: customer impact, revenue lift, and risk. both are important; observability tops short-term list because it reduces regressions in production.

[15:00] Q&A wrap-up.

[15:10] Caroline: I'll publish the feature timelines and a short FAQ on Private GA tomorrow.

[15:20] Tom: I'll follow up with perf numbers and a tech note.

[15:30] Sara: People will share hiring tracker and interview matrix.

[15:40] Maya: thanks all. closing notes: big thanks. we'll follow up in Slack with links and the recording.

[15:55] End of meeting — casual drop-in chat for leadership linger took ~10 minutes more but not recorded here.
